web-client.description: React frontend (TypeScript). Handles login UI, session state, access token storage and refresh flow on page load.

api-auth.description: Express API auth controllers and token service. Issues JWTs, handles refresh-token grant, validates tokens.

token-persistence.description: Refresh token repository (DB layer) and DB migrations. Stores, looks up and invalidates refresh tokens.

entry_points: demo-app/web/src/lib/session.ts — initSession() called on page load, decides whether to redirect to login
demo-app/api/src/controllers/refreshController.ts — POST /refresh, consumes refresh token and issues new access token
bug_flow: On page load the client checks if the access token is still valid. If expired, it should silently exchange the refresh token via POST /refresh for a new access token and stay logged in. Instead users end up on the login page with no error, suggesting the refresh either silently fails, is never attempted, or the redirect-to-login decision fires before the refresh completes.

investigation_scopes.name: client
investigation_scopes.why: The symptom is a silent redirect to login. The client session-init and token-refresh logic is the first place to look for why the refresh is not attempted or why the redirect fires too early.

investigation_scopes.name: refresh-api
investigation_scopes.why: If the client does call /refresh, the API could be returning an error (silently to the user) due to token validation, expiry logic, or error handling that does not propagate correctly.

investigation_scopes.name: token-store
investigation_scopes.why: The refresh token must exist and not be expired in the DB for the exchange to succeed. The DB schema, rotation/deletion logic and expiry values directly affect whether the refresh succeeds or silently fails when users return after a while.
